LESSON: THREE- DIMENSION (3- D) OBJECTS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Geometry
Topic 3.3: Three- Dimension (3- D) Objects
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Three- Dimension (3- D) Objects, part of Geometry in Grade 5 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: Where are 3-D objects used in the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. share tasks with peers to identify, collect objects and discuss cubes, cuboids, cylinders, spheres and pyramids as 3-D objects in the environment,

2. watch a video on 3-D objects,

3. describe 2-D shapes found in 3-D objects and share with other groups,

4. use digital devices and other resources to draw and learn more about 3-D objects.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. share tasks with peers to identify, collect objects and discuss cubes, cuboids, cylinders, spheres and pyramids as 3-D objects in the environment,
2. watch a video on 3-D objects,
3. describe 2-D shapes found in 3-D objects and share with other groups,
4. use digital devices and other resources to draw and learn more about 3-D objects.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Three- Dimension (3- D) Objects together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Responsibility: learner shares tasks with peers while identifying and collecting 3-D objects in the environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental awareness: learner identifies and collects 3-D objects in the environment.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of 3-D objects and 2-D shapes to modelling in Creative Arts.
